restrictions: Messages are uniformly random 64-byte strings; each is one SHA3-256 block. No permutation call is used: every hash is computed by a charged bitsliced program, 256 messages per 256-bit word.

The hash program is a fixed straight-line sequence of 70,772 instructions per 256 messages using 15 of 16 registers of a 256-bit machine (41,266 ALU, 18,290 loads, 11,216 stores), executed and checked against the reference in experiments/keccak_bitslice.py.
Fixed work: q = 2^128 messages, 3-pass LSD radix sort (digits 86/85/85 bits), one scan; 92,537/256 = 361.47 charged word operations per message at 1/C, C = 1626.
One-time program construction is charged as preprocessing (below 2^40 operations), included in time.
Success >= 0.3934 is proved for the fixed target via Schur-concavity of the birthday probability (Munford 1977); no randomness heuristic.
Memory 2^135.81 bytes (plane archive, key and record arrays, counters); reported, not scored.
